summary: Sister Vajirā (1928–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Paul Debes and under Narada Maha Thera in 1955.
Sita Krishna Nambiar works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Paul Hacker.

Sita Ram Roy, a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology, studied under doctoral supervisors Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma (1962). He held posts at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Bihar (attested 1971), and Gaya Museum (attested 1971).
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005 and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indology scholar who served as a Sanskrit teacher at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, where his posts are attested in 1892 and 1929.
Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was a history and archaeology scholar. He was educated at Tsinghua University and Harvard University, where he studied from circa 1925 to 1930.

So Takahashi (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Meijo University, where he was an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991).

Sodo Mori (born 1934) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Kogen Mizuno, Hajime Nakamura, and Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera. He held professorships at Josai University and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure. He studied under Ekō Hashimoto and trained at Antai-ji under Kodo Sawaki from 1949 to 1957, later teaching Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies master. Educated at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo (circa 1927–1930), he studied under Gempo Yamamoto from circa 1931 to 1961 and taught students including Philip Kapleau and Robert Baker Aitken.

Sogaku Daiun Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, training under Dokutan Sōsan and Sodo Kakusho Harada, among others. He was a professor at Komazawa University (1911–1923) and taught Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Nihon University. He taught Yamada Koun and held a post at Kanagawa University.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) was a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Nihon University. He served as abbot at Kobo-in, taught at Hanazono University—serving as president from 1978 to 1982—and founded Chozen-ji and Seitai-ji.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge. He studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse, and founded Rigpa in 1975.
Sohanwela Pemarathana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the National University of Singapore under the thesis supervision of Saranindranath Tagore (attested 2004).

Soiku Shigematsu (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Kyoto University, and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships in English literature at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies figure. He served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996), teaching Yoel Hoffmann and Sonja Arntzen.

Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied under Kosen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893), founded Ryōbōkai and Ningen Zen Kyodan, and taught Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts and under Sokatsu Shaku. He founded the Buddhist Society of America in 1930 and taught Alan Watts and Ruth Fuller Sasaki.

Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961) was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology who studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō. He held posts at the SMR Research Department (circa 1908–1919), Waseda University (circa 1920–1940), and the University of Tokyo.
